primary_sources.title: Manifold-constrained plasticity enables stable learning in recurrent neural circuits

verified_observations: Reviewer #1 explicitly asked for drift as a sequence of small incremental rotations of the population activity manifold, describing the biologically relevant regime as rotation of the entire manifold with neurons dropping in and out of the active population, and separately requested a reaching-task test on a rotated non-stationary target manifold.
The accepted article labels the added section 'Online subspace tracking stabilizes learning under coordinate rotation' and labels S8A as a 'rotation of the manifold coordinates'.

The article earlier distinguishes within-manifold perturbations as orthogonal remapping of latent coordinates inside the intrinsic activity subspace from outside-manifold perturbations that rotate a basis toward directions orthogonal to the manifold.

The article states that its gradual rotational-drift update evolves an orthonormal manifold basis with a rotation matrix and an incremental rotation angle, and later interprets S11 as frozen versus adaptive alignment to an 'evolving population subspace'.

The article's principal-angle metric is computed from empirical activity bases obtained by SVD over activity windows, not directly from the imposed structural basis; the paper itself says this metric captures empirical covariance drift and not displacement relative to the imposed structural subspace.

independent_algebraic_check.condition: For the worker-reported Eq.34 form Q_next = Q R with Q in R^(N x k) orthonormal and R in R^(k x k) orthogonal
independent_algebraic_check.result: The structural projector is exactly invariant: (Q R)(Q R)^T = Q R R^T Q^T = Q Q^T. The k-dimensional structural span therefore does not rotate into new ambient dimensions under that right action.

scope_conclusion.supported: The published S8-S12 suite supports a claim about tracking empirical activity/covariance changes induced under a coordinate-rotation / within-manifold remapping regime, and about adaptive Oja tracking outperforming a frozen estimated basis in that regime.
scope_conclusion.not_supported: The published text alone does not establish performance when the structural k-dimensional manifold itself rotates into new ambient neural dimensions while the alarm, recurrent construction, projection semantics, rank and noise regime are otherwise held fixed.
scope_conclusion.material_reason: The review requested an ambient/non-stationary manifold-rotation regime, whereas the final paper explicitly describes coordinate rotation; under the worker-reported right-rotation equation the structural projector is invariant. A high empirical S11 principal angle can still arise from empirical covariance/rank/noise/dynamics effects because Eq.37 measures an activity-derived subspace, but it is not direct evidence that the structural span Q Q^T rotated.

unresolved: S1 Code (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002) is linked by PLOS, but the binary redirect could not be recovered through the available read-only transport in this run; code semantics were therefore not independently inspected.

The exact rendered symbolic Eq.34 could not be extracted from the HTML text because PLOS exposes it as an image; the right-rotation algebra above is conditional on the exact worker-transcribed formula and should be upgraded to direct code/XML verification when transport permits.
The page is explicitly marked 'uncorrected proof'; any later Version of Record correction should be rechecked before treating this audit as final-publication provenance.

Without code, it remains unresolved whether W is rebuilt as Q changes, how W_k transforms, whether recurrent state/input/noise are explicitly projected through Q Q^T at every step, the exact U initialization/freeze schedule, and the exact S11 principal-angle operands/rank handling.
